'''Kalman Varga''' is a Hungarian-American physicist, currently at [[Vanderbilt University]]. He researches [[nanoscience|computational nanoscience]], focusing on developing novel computational methods for electronic structure calculations. He is an Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://as.vanderbilt.edu/physics/bio/kalman-varga |title=Kalman Varga |publisher=vanderbilt.edu |accessdate=April 22, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |title=Fellows |publisher=aps.org |accessdate=April 22, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=K4PJuBUAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Kalman Varga |accessdate=April 22, 2017}}</ref> He was accredited to co-writing ''Computational Nanoscience: Applications for Molecules, Clusters, and Solids'' in 2011, as well as  ''Structure and Reactions of Light Exotic Nuclei'' (2003), and ''Stochastic Variational Approach to Quantum-Mechanical Few-Body Problems'' (1998).
